threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 'secret' vinyl shop down the alley is a hidden gem, but we all know it's just the latest tourist trap.
Last night on the 3 bus, a guy serenaded everyone with a 90s R&B tune. Not a soul complained, just a few off-key backup singers joining in.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was home when I spotted a local cat casually sunbathing on a makeshift throne of beer crates outside a Späti.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a döner at 4 AM, then stumble into a spontaneous street party with DJs and live murals. Never a dull night here.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their annoyance at BART delays yet knowing the best taco truck to hit while waiting.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the bus when a random dog decided to lounge on the tracks—only in SF do passengers applaud when it finally moves.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all street performers are just fun, but some are loud enough to invade quiet corners where locals seek peace.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They're the ones still staring at the street signs, trying to decipher the Catalan version of their way to the metro.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused when the bus doesn’t stop at the curb and the driver just waves you on. We’ve all been there.
Caught a late-night bus and saw a guy offering free hugs near the market. He was surprisingly popular, must've given out at least thirty before it hit midnight.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a guy on the corner selling homemade falafel from a bicycle at 2 AM, I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you enjoy a late-night döner kebab while listening to street performers rap in German, blending cultures right on the sidewalk.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a true local when they don’t flinch at the smell of sourdough but wrinkle their nose at the whiff of a freshly opened kombucha.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the Civic Center bus stuck behind a yoga class blocking the intersection. Only in SF do we need to navigate traffic around downward dogs.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always miss that Gràcia’s plazas are vibrant at dusk. They flock to the touristy spots while we enjoy spontaneous concerts and local chatter.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by how they struggle with the 'x' in 'coca de llardons'—the locals roll it off the tongue like it's second nature.
